course.title: Math III-Discrete Mathematics
course.description: This course is an introduction to discrete mathematics for computer science, data science and engineering. It emphasizes mathematical definitions and proofs as well as applicable methods. Topics include formal logic notation, proof methods, induction, elementary number theory, and elementary graph theory and real life applications.

clos.description: Apply a wide range of principles of discrete mathematics, such as problem solving, and mathematical proofs and reasoning to solve real world problems
Apply elementary number theory in public key cryptography and graph theory in graph coloring and matching
Demonstrate effective communication of reasoning, solutions, and interpretations through oral and written presentations
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Project Reports, Project Presentations, Peer evaluation (FA)

clos.description: Use mathematical software (such as Python or Mathematica) with proficiency to simulate RSA cryptosystem, graph coloring and matching

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction Course orientation Logics Truth tables
topics.llosRaw: -LLO1: Identify mathematical statements as propositions or non-propositions -LLO2: Use truth tables to deal with logical statements -LLO3: Apply logical reasoning to determine the truth value of a logical statement

topics.title: Topic 2: Propositional logic
topics.llosRaw: -LLO1: Analyze compound propositions using logical connectives -LLO2: Apply truth table and logical rules to show logical equivalences

topics.title: Topic 3: Methods of Proofs Direct proofs Indirect proofs
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Apply basic principles of logic to construct simple proofs - LLO2: Apply various methods of proof to prove mathematical statements

topics.title: Topic 4: Induction Induction Invariant
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Explain the main steps of mathematical induction - LLO2: Apply the principle of mathematical induction to prove statements involving natural numbers

topics.title: Topic 5: Strong Induction Strong induction Well ordering principle
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Justify proofs using variants of induction (such as strong induction) to establish the correctness of recursively defined statements - LLO2: Connect well ordering principle to strong induction

topics.title: Topic 6: Euclid’s Algorithm Divisibility Euclid’s Algorithm
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Apply Euclid’s Algorithm to compute the greatest common divisor (GCD) of integers efficiently - LLO2: Use the Extended Euclidean Algorithm to compute modular inverses for encryption and decryption processes

topics.title: Topic 7: Modular Arithmetic
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Apply modular arithmetic operations to simplify computations relevant to cryptographic algorithms - LLO2: Compute modular inverses

topics.title: Topic 8: Euler’s Function
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Compute Euler’s totient function for integers using prime factorization - LLO1: Apply Euler’s theorem to solve problems arising in public key cryptography

topics.title: Topic 9: Secret Sharing and Public Key Cryptography
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Explain the number-theoretic foundations of public key cryptography to implement basic encryption and decryption procedures - LLO2: Construct simple secret sharing RSA schemes by using modular arithmetic - LLO3: Evaluate the correctness and security principles of RSA public key cryptography

topics.title: Topic 10: Graph Theory
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Explain the basic properties of graphs - LLO2: Describe different types of graphs such as simple, multigraphs, directed graphs - LLO3: Interpret structural properties of graphs such as degree, paths, cycles, and connectivity

topics.title: Topic 11: Graph Coloring
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Compute chromatic numbers of graphs - LLO2: Apply graph coloring techniques to determine proper colorings

topics.title: Topic 12: Matching
topics.llosRaw: - LLO1: Solve matching problems in graphs by identifying matchings, maximum matchings, and perfect matchings - LLO2: Justify solutions using graph-theoretic arguments

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
